summary: Define fully-typed application settings with Pydantic, load configuration from YAML, TOML, JSON, or .env files, and retrieve a cached instance with a single call. Template strings let you derive fields from other fields automatically. Connection profiles give you ready-made typed settings for databases, storage backends, and APIs, with built-in support for the authentication mode your target expects.
use_cases: Configure a data pipeline that reads connection details from a YAML file and resolves secrets from Vault at startup
Build a CLI application where environment variables override file-based defaults, with template-derived output paths
Set up a multi-environment project where dev, staging, and production each have their own config files merged in priority order
Define a reusable database connection profile that auto-derives connection strings from individual host, port, and database fields

concepts.name: Defining a settings class
concepts.description: Subclass MountainAshBaseSettings to declare your application's configuration as typed Python fields. Pydantic validation ensures every value meets your constraints as soon as the settings object is created. Use post_init() to compute any fields that depend on other values.

concepts.name: Loading configuration files
concepts.description: Pass one or more file paths to config_files and the framework loads YAML, TOML, JSON, or .env files automatically based on extension. For advanced scenarios, SettingsParameters.create() lets you compose file lists, environment overrides, and kwargs into a single merged configuration.

concepts.name: Template-driven derived fields
concepts.description: Use {FIELD_NAME} syntax in default values to build fields that derive their value from other settings. Combined with the UPath / operator, this makes cross-platform path construction straightforward and declarative.

concepts.name: Getting cached settings instances
concepts.description: Call get_settings() to retrieve a cached, ready-to-use settings instance. Structural parameters (files, env prefix) determine the cache key, while runtime parameters (per-call overrides) are applied on top of the cached base, keeping startup fast and memory efficient.

concepts.name: Merging settings parameters
concepts.description: SettingsParameters.create() and merge() combine multiple configuration sources with clear priority rules. File lists are unioned, scalar values follow last-wins, and dictionaries are deep-merged, giving you predictable multi-layer configuration composition.

concepts.name: Secrets resolution
concepts.description: Register a secrets provider (Vault, SSM, KeyVault, or your own) and reference secrets in config files or kwargs with the secret:path/to/value prefix. The framework resolves secrets transparently during settings construction, so your application code works with plain typed values.

concepts.name: Building connection profiles
concepts.description: Declare a ProfileDescriptor listing the parameters your connection needs, then subclass DescriptorProfile to get a fully-typed settings class with those fields wired in automatically. Register profiles in a Registry so downstream code can look them up by name.

concepts.name: Authentication modes
concepts.description: Choose from built-in auth modes including password, token, OAuth2, IAM, service account, Azure AD, and more. Each mode is an AuthSpec subclass selected via a kind literal field, so your configuration is explicit about which credentials are expected and how they are supplied.
